type.text: Public land-grant research university; the flagship of the University of Maine System.

size.text: 8,225 undergraduates and 10,644 students overall in fall 2025; the separately reported Machias regional campus is not included.

campus.text: The main campus is in Orono, Maine, near Bangor. Campus walking tours cover gardens, public art, the central mall, and the historic district.

housing.text: On-campus residence halls include living-learning communities. Housing options include traditional rooms and suites; campus meal plans cover dining halls and other meal options.

studentLife.text: More than 200 student clubs cover academic interests, service, media, arts, and leadership.

recreation.text: The Black Bears compete in NCAA Division I. The New Balance Recreation Center offers aquatics, intramurals, wellness activities, and outdoor adventure programs.

photo.alt: Aerial view of the University of Maine campus in Orono in autumn.

type.text: Public land-grant research university and the flagship campus of the University of Massachusetts system.

size.text: 24,019 undergraduates and 7,299 graduate students in fall 2025, including University Without Walls students. These are university-wide figures.

campus.text: The Amherst campus covers approximately 1,450 acres in western Massachusetts’ Pioneer Valley, with academic buildings, residential areas, the campus pond, and the W. E. B. Du Bois Library.

housing.text: Students live in on-campus residential communities or off campus. Campus dining includes dining commons, cafés, and food options in the Campus Center.

studentLife.text: More than 300 registered student organizations include arts, cultural groups, community service, Greek life, and club sports.

recreation.text: Campus recreation includes a recreation center and intramural sports leagues. UMass also competes in NCAA Division I athletics.

photo.alt: W. E. B. Du Bois Library, the Campus Center, and campus pond at UMass Amherst.

type.text: Independent university with undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs in the sciences, arts, business, and health professions.

size.text: 2,139 undergraduate students by headcount in the fall 2025 university snapshot; graduate and professional students are reported separately.

campus.text: Undergraduate campus life is based in Biddeford, Maine, beside the Saco River and Atlantic coast. UNE also has campuses in Portland, Maine, and Tangier, Morocco.

housing.text: First-year residence halls and upperclass suite-style housing are available. The Danielle N. Ripich Commons combines dining, study space, and student services overlooking the Saco River.

studentLife.text: More than 100 student clubs and organizations include academic and cultural groups, hobbies, and student government. Campus events also take place in the Commons and residence halls.

recreation.text: Biddeford facilities include two fitness centers, an indoor pool, an ice rink, tennis and basketball courts, and outdoor equipment rentals; students can also join club and intramural sports.

photo.alt: UNE students playing pool and foosball in the Biddeford campus Commons.

type.text: Public research university offering undergraduate, graduate, and professional study.

size.text: More than 15,000 undergraduates in the university’s current admissions overview; graduate students are additional.

campus.text: The 1,200-acre Kingston campus is in southern Rhode Island, about 30 miles south of Providence and near ocean beaches. Its historic core sits alongside newer academic buildings.

housing.text: On-campus housing and dining are available, alongside off-campus living. University housing and dining pages describe the current residential and meal options.

studentLife.text: More than 120 student organizations include cycling, sailing, poetry, and meditation. Student media, Greek life, student senate, volunteering, and leadership programs are also available.

recreation.text: Students can participate in recreational activities, intramural and club sports, or follow URI’s varsity athletics teams.

photo.alt: Aerial view of the University of Rhode Island Kingston campus and quadrangle.

type.text: Jesuit university offering undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. Its educational tradition includes service and engagement with the wider community.

size.text: 2,492 students in the university’s published at-a-glance profile. The profile does not specify an enrollment year.

campus.text: The 72-acre campus is in Buffalo, New York, within an urban setting.

housing.text: Campus housing includes five residence halls and living-learning communities. Commuter services and campus dining are also provided.

studentLife.text: Student organizations cover music, service, advocacy, gaming, and other interests; campus life also includes student government, leadership activities, Greek life, and campus ministry.

recreation.text: The Golden Griffins compete in NCAA Division I. Students can also join club sports and intramural leagues or use campus fitness facilities.

photo.alt: Aerial view of Canisius University and surrounding Buffalo neighborhoods in autumn.

type.text: Public research university with land-, sea-, and space-grant missions.

size.text: More than 11,250 undergraduates and 2,500 graduate students in the university’s current facts profile. These are university-wide figures.

campus.text: Zoology is based at the main residential campus in Durham, New Hampshire. College Woods provides 250 acres of woods, fields, and streams for teaching, research, and recreation.

housing.text: Campus living includes residence halls and dining facilities. The Memorial Union Building is a gathering place for events and everyday student activities.

studentLife.text: More than 200 student-run clubs and organizations cover a range of interests. The Memorial Union Building hosts student activities and social spaces.

recreation.text: UNH has NCAA Division I athletics, club sports, and campus recreation. College Woods is also used for walking, running, and cross-country skiing.

photo.alt: Thompson Hall and the University of New Hampshire campus in Durham.

type.text: Private university with undergraduate and graduate study; experiential education is part of its institution-wide curriculum.

size.text: 1,768 undergraduates and 431 graduate students, for 2,199 total students in the fall 2024 institutional report.

campus.text: Located in Doylestown, Pennsylvania, in Bucks County, about 30 miles north of Philadelphia. The surrounding area includes museums, historic buildings, parks, and trails.

housing.text: Campus housing and dining serve residential students, with separate information and services for commuters. Residence options and the residency policy are described on the housing page.

studentLife.text: The fall 2024 report lists 71 student clubs and organizations. Music, arts, campus events, and student activities are part of campus life.

recreation.text: Students can participate in NCAA Division III athletics or intramural teams. Nearby parks offer hiking, biking, and other outdoor recreation.

photo.alt: Delaware Valley University students working together in the South Residence Hall lobby.

uma-bangor.name: University of Maine at Augusta · Bangor campus

type.text: University of Maine System institution with campuses in Augusta and Bangor, regional locations, and online programs. The student body includes recent high-school graduates and returning adults.

size.text: 4,336 students university-wide in fall 2025, including 1,262 Early College students. This includes online and other locations; it is not a Bangor-campus headcount.

campus.text: The Bangor campus is across from Bangor International Airport, with access from I-95. Facilities include specialized labs and clinics, study spaces, and the Nottage Library.

housing.text: Limited housing for eligible full-time Bangor students is arranged at a local Holiday Inn, with a campus shuttle. Meal plans are available; a housing application does not guarantee a space.

studentLife.text: The Bangor Student Life office and Student Government Association organize activities, trips, and leadership opportunities. Student events include music, talks, and campus gatherings.

recreation.text: The Bangor Fitness Center has a gymnasium, weights, cardio equipment, and pickup basketball, pickleball, and floorball. Student access is free.

photo.alt: A student beside the University of Maine at Augusta Bangor campus entrance sign.

type.text: Public college of technology in the State University of New York system, offering associate and bachelor’s degrees as well as certificates.

size.text: 2,833 undergraduate students in fall 2025. The institutional-research count excludes auditors, cross-registered students, and College in the High School students.

campus.text: A 555-acre campus beside the Grasse River in Canton, northern New York. Footbridges connect campus with the village; walking, running, biking, and ski trails surround the grounds.

housing.text: On-campus options include traditional residence halls and apartment-style suites in Kennedy Hall. Residential students have campus meal plans.

studentLife.text: Student organizations include academic clubs, service groups, cultural organizations, and outdoor activities. Campus events include performances, trips, festivals, and student-government activities.

recreation.text: NCAA Division III athletics, intramurals, and esports are available. Recreation facilities include an ice rink, pool, fitness center, and field house.

photo.alt: SUNY Canton students walking through the campus plaza after class.

type.text: Public technology college in the State University of New York system, offering associate, bachelor’s, and master’s degrees, plus certificates.

size.text: Approximately 3,300 students overall in the college’s fall 2026 enrollment announcement. This is the college-wide total.

campus.text: Located in the village of Delhi in New York’s Catskill Mountains. The college serves residential, commuter, and online students.

housing.text: Campus residence halls include traditional rooms and upper-division options; Riverview Townhouses provide another upper-division community. Campus dining services are available during the semester.

studentLife.text: Student clubs and organizations, community service, and student-government leadership provide activities outside classes.

recreation.text: The Broncos compete in NCAA Division III. Students also have intramurals, fitness activities, and marked campus trails for walking, running, and cycling.

photo.alt: Aerial view of SUNY Delhi’s campus among the Catskill hills.

campus.text: Veterinary Technology students spend years 1–2 in Amherst and years 3–4 at the Charles River Campus in Newton. Amherst has approximately 1,450 acres; the Newton campus has 66 acres in a suburban setting near Boston.

housing.text: Amherst offers on-campus residential communities and dining commons. At Charles River, students have residence halls, campus dining, free parking, and transportation to the MBTA Green Line.

studentLife.text: Amherst has more than 300 registered student organizations. At Charles River, a separate Student Life office organizes student engagement and activities for residential and commuter students.

recreation.text: Amherst has a recreation center, intramural leagues, and NCAA Division I athletics. Charles River has a fitness center, outdoor recreation facilities, and nature trails.
